STUDYQURAN:9:75/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r1.claim: Like other descriptions of hypocrites in this sūrah, these verses are understood generally.
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r1.anchor: As with other descriptions of the hypocrites in this sūrah, these verses are understood in a general sense

STUDYQURAN:9:75/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r2.claim: Some commentators connect the passage with Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib, who promised charity if wealthy, prospered after receiving spoils, moved away, gradually stopped congregational and Friday prayers, then refused zakāh as jizyah; the Prophet rebuked him.
STUDYQURAN:9:75/r2.anchor: some commentators also connect them with a certain Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib

TAB-FULL:v11p576/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r2.claim: Once God gave them wealth, they withheld charity, refused to maintain relatives, and did not spend for God; they turned away from their covenant.
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r2.anchor: بفضل الله الذي آتاهم فلم يصدقوا منه ولم يصلوا منه قرابة ولم ينفقوا منه في حق الله

TAB-FULL:v11p576/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r3.claim: Their turning away and being averse refers to turning away from the covenant they had made with God.
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r3.anchor: وأدبروا عن عهدهم الذي عاهدوه الله

TAB-FULL:v11p576/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man as the Anṣārī Thaʿlaba b. Ḥāṭib, who publicly pledged charity, giving each person their due, and maintaining kin; after receiving wealth he broke his promise, angered God, and his story was revealed in these verses.
TAB-FULL:v11p576/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله

TAB-FULL:v11p579/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r1.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r1.claim: Thalaba says he asked for wealth, promised to give every rightful person his due, and the Prophet prayed for him after his pledge.
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r1.anchor: عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري، أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادع الله أن يرزقني مالا

TAB-FULL:v11p579/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r2.claim: The Prophet warned Thalaba that a little wealth whose thanks he could render was better than much wealth he could not bear.
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ويحك يا ثعلبة، قليل تؤدي شكره، خير من كثير لا تطيقه»

TAB-FULL:v11p579/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r3.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r3.claim: Thalaba's growing flock forced him out of Medina; he gradually left congregational prayers and eventually even Friday prayer, asking travelers for news.
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r3.anchor: عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري، أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادع الله أن يرزقني مالا

TAB-FULL:v11p579/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r5.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r5.claim: After the verses about his broken pledge were revealed, Thalaba begged the Prophet to accept his charity, but the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman refused; he died during Uthman's caliphate.
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r5.anchor: فخرج ثعلبة حتى أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فسأله أن يقبل منه صدقته

TAB-FULL:v11p581/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r1.claim: Qatada reports that an Ansari at an assembly vowed to give every rightful person his due if God granted wealth, but acted otherwise when wealth came.
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله الآية: ذكر لنا أن رجلا من الأنصار

TAB-FULL:v11p581/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r2.claim: The Prophet recounted that Israelites asked Moses for a manageable set of commands instead of following the Torah while pursuing livelihoods; God gave them three commands, which they soon neglected.
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r2.anchor: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حدث أن موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام لما جاء بالتوراة

TAB-FULL:v11p581/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r3.claim: The Prophet promised Paradise to those who would not lie, break promises, or betray trusts and who guarded their eyes, hands, and private parts from betrayal, theft, and adultery.
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r3.anchor: قالوا: ما هن يا رسول الله؟ قال: «إذا حدثتم فلا تكذبوا، وإذا وعدتم فلا تخلفوا

TAB-FULL:v11p581/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says three traits mark a hypocrite even if he fasts, prays, and claims Islam: lying, betraying a trust, and breaking a promise.
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: " ثلاث من كن فيه صار منافقا

TAB-FULL:v11p581/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r5.claim: Other authorities identify the two people behind the pledge as Thalaba and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.
TAB-FULL:v11p581/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل المعني بذلك: رجلان: أحدهما ثعلبة، والآخر معتب بن قشير

TAB-FULL:v11p583/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the pledge-makers as Thalaba ibn Hatib and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, both from Banu Amr ibn Awf.
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن عبيد، عن الحسن: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله}

TAB-FULL:v11p583/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r2.claim: Mujahid says two men left an assembled group after swearing that they would give charity if God granted them wealth, but withheld it when enriched.
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله}

TAB-FULL:v11p583/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes them as a class of hypocrites whose withholding caused hypocrisy to remain in their hearts until meeting God, without repentance, forgiveness, or pardon, as with Iblis.
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r3.anchor: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله}

TAB-FULL:v11p583/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says the verse makes broken promises and lying a sign of hypocrisy, an understanding also held by Companions and Successors and supported by reports from the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r4.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر: في هذه الآية الإبانة من الله جل ثناؤه عن علامة أهل النفاق

TAB-FULL:v11p583/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r5.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r5.claim: Abdullah says a hypocrite is recognized by lying, breaking promises, and treachery in a pact, and recites this passage as confirmation.
TAB-FULL:v11p583/r5.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن عمارة، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، قال: قال عبد الله: " اعتبروا المنافق بثلاث: إذا حدث كذب

TAB-FULL:v11p586/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says three traits make a person a hypocrite: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying a trust; he recites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r1.anchor: عن صبيح بن عبد الله بن عميرة، عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: " ثلاث من كن فيه كان منافقا: إذا حدث كذب

TAB-FULL:v11p586/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says he eventually found hypocrisy's three signs—lying, breaking promises, and betrayal—in this passage and in the verse about the Trust offered to heaven and earth.
TAB-FULL:v11p586/r2.anchor: قال: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي، يقول: " كنت أسمع أن المنافق يعرف بثلاث: بالكذب، والإخلاف، والخيانة

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r1.claim: A report through al-Hasan attributes to the Prophet the saying that lying, betrayal of trust, and breaking a promise mark a hypocrite even if he prays, fasts, and claims Islam.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r1.anchor: سمعت الحسن، يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ثلاث من كن فيه فهو منافق وإن صلى

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r2.claim: Asked whether promising repayment while temporarily unable to pay makes him a hypocrite, al-Hasan answers that this is how the hadith was transmitted.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r2.anchor: فقلت للحسن: يا أبا سعيد لئن كان لرجل علي دين فلقيني، فتقاضاني وليس عندي، وخفت أن يحبسني ويهلكني

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan recounts that Abdullah ibn Amr's father fulfilled a promise to marry a man to his daughter on his deathbed so he would not meet God with a third of hypocrisy.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r3.anchor: ثم حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن أباه لما حضره الموت، قال: زوجوا فلانا فإني وعدته أن أزوجه

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r4.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r4.claim: Ata argues that Yusuf's brothers lied, broke a promise, and betrayed trust without being hypocrites, since their father and grandfather were prophets; this challenges treating the traits as universal proof of hypocrisy.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r4.anchor: عطاء بن أبي رباح، فأخبرته الحديث الذي سمعته من الحسن، وبالذي قلت له وقال لي فقال: أعجزت أن تقول له: أخبرني عن إخوة يوسف

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r5.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet's three traits concerned hypocrites who lied to him, betrayed his confidential trust, and broke their pledge to campaign; a spy disclosed Abu Sufyan's location, occasioning 8:27 and 9:75–77.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r5.anchor: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما قال هذا الحديث في المنافقين خاصة

TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan agrees that Ata correctly traced the hadith's origin and that its three traits apply specifically to hypocrites.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r6.anchor: فأخذ الحسن بيدي فأمالها وقال: يا أهل العراق أعجزتم أن تكونوا مثل هذا؟ سمع مني حديثا فلم يقبله حتى استنبط أصله

TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet's saying that lying, breaking promises, and betraying trusts make one a hypocrite, even if one prays, fasts, and claims Islam.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ثلاث من كن فيه وإن صلى وصام وزعم أنه مسلم فهو منافق

TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن وائل
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r2.claim: On his deathbed, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il said he had nearly promised a suitor his daughter and formally married her to him to avoid meeting God with a third of hypocrisy.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r2.anchor: عن هارون بن رئاب، عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن وائل أنه لما حضرته الوفاة

TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r3.speaker: قوم
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r3.claim: Some say the pledge-makers only intended their vow inwardly and never spoke it aloud.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: كان العهد الذي عاهد الله هؤلاء المنافقون شيئا نووه في أنفسهم ولم يتكلموا به

TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r4.speaker: معتمر بن سليمان التيمي
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r4.claim: Mu'tamir recounts forming an unspoken vow during a storm at sea; when he consulted his father Sulayman, his father told him to voice or fulfill it.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r4.anchor: سمعت معتمر بن سليمان التيمي، يقول: «ركبت البحر فأصابنا ريح شديدة، فنذر قوم منا نذورا

TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r5.speaker: سعيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r5.claim: Said ibn Thabit says the vow was an inward intention not spoken aloud, citing God's knowledge of people's secrets and private conversations.
TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن ثابت، قال: قوله: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله} [التوبة: 75] الآية، قال: إنما هو شيء نووه

TABATABAI:9:75-77/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r1.claim: One group of poor hypocrites promised to give charity and be righteous if enriched, then became miserly and turned away when God gave them wealth; other hypocrites criticized both affluent and poor believers who donated, and God judged them all hypocrites and beyond forgiveness.
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r1.anchor: بيان تذكر الآيات طائفة أخرى من المنافقين تخلفوا عن حكم الصدقات فامتنعوا عن إيتاء الزكاة

TABATABAI:9:75-77/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r3.claim: The context presents a real event, and the reports say these verses were revealed about Tha'laba; the author defers the story to the following report discussion and says the verses' meaning is clear.
TABATABAI:9:75-77/r3.anchor: والروايات تدل على أن الآيات نزلت في ثعلبة في قصة سيأتي نقلها في البحث الروائي التالي

TABRISI:9:75-78/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:75-78/r2.claim: Bukhil originally means refusing a petitioner because giving feels difficult; religious usage applies it to withholding an obligation such as zakat.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r2.anchor: والبخل منع السائل لشدة الإعطاء ثم صار في الشرع لمنع الواجب لأن من منع الزكاة فهو بخيل

TABRISI:9:75-78/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r3.speaker: الرماني
TABRISI:9:75-78/r3.claim: Al-Rummani rejects defining stinginess as withholding an obligation because giving is difficult: then generosity would mean discharging an obligation without difficulty, making a person who pays a debt generous.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r3.anchor: قال الرماني لا يجوز أن يكون البخل منع الواجب لمشقة الإعطاء

TABRISI:9:75-78/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r4.speaker: زهير
TABRISI:9:75-78/r4.claim: Zuhayr's poem calls the miser blameworthy wherever he may be and the generous person praiseworthy despite circumstances.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r4.anchor:
كما قال زهير:
إن البخيل ملوم حيث كان ول

TABRISI:9:75-78/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r5.speaker: الرماني
TABRISI:9:75-78/r5.claim: Al-Rummani defines stinginess as withholding what causes no harm if given and no benefit if retained when wisdom calls for giving; the refusal reflects tightness of spirit even without material harm.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r5.anchor: ومن منع ما لا يضره بذله ولا ينفعه منعه مما تدعو إليه الحكمة فهو بخيل لأنه لا يقع المنع على هذه الصفة

TABRISI:9:75-78/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:75-78/r8.claim: Lamma is like idha here; unlike future-oriented in and idha, lamma and lawla concern what has passed, with lamma indicating that the second event occurred because the first did.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r8.anchor: معنى لما معنى إذا لأن لما الغالب عليها الجزاء وهي اسم يقع في جواب متى يقال متى كان كذا

TABRISI:9:75-78/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-78/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:75-78/r9.claim: The second object of “gave them from His bounty” is omitted; the implied object is what they had requested from His bounty.
TABRISI:9:75-78/r9.anchor: فلما آتاهم من فضله المفعول الثاني محذوف تقديره فلما آتاهم ما تمنوه من فضله

TABRISI:9:75-77/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-77/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
TABRISI:9:75-77/r1.claim: A report attributed to Abu Umama and raised to the Prophet tells of Thalaba's repeated request for wealth, broken charity pledge, neglect of communal worship, and refusal to pay, after which the Prophet lamented him.
TABRISI:9:75-77/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي وروي ذلك مرفوعا

TABRISI:9:75-77/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:75-77/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:75-77/r7.claim: When God granted the wealth they desired, they withheld it and its due from God, turned away from His command, and were averse to His religion.
TABRISI:9:75-77/r7.anchor: عن الوفاء بالعهد ومنعوا حق الله منه

THALABI:v5p72/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p72/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p72/r1.claim: The report says collectors brought the Prophet's letter to Tha'laba, who twice called zakat a jizya and delayed; al-Sulami gave his best camels willingly, and the Prophet blessed him while lamenting Tha'laba after revelation of the promise passage.
THALABI:v5p72/r1.anchor: فخرجا حتى أتيا ثعلبة فسألاه الصدقة وقرءا له كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال:

THALABI:v5p72/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p72/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p72/r2.claim: When Tha'laba later offered the charity, the Prophet said God had forbidden him to accept it and rebuked him for disobeying the instruction he had been given.
THALABI:v5p72/r2.anchor: فقال: «إن الله تعالى منعني أن أقبل منك صدقتك» فجعل يحثي على رأسه التراب

THALABI:v5p72/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p72/r3.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان
THALABI:v5p72/r3.claim: After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman each refused Tha'laba's repeated offers because the Prophet had rejected them; Tha'laba died during Uthman's caliphate.
THALABI:v5p72/r3.anchor: فقال أبو بكر: لم يقبلها منك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا أقبلها؟ فلم يقبل

THALABI:v5p73/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p73/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Umar through Masruq attributes to the Prophet four marks of complete hypocrisy and says any one persists as a mark until abandoned: lying, breaking promises, betraying covenants, and obscene conduct in dispute.
THALABI:v5p73/r1.anchor: عن مسروق عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أربع من كن فيه

THALABI:v5p73/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p73/r2.claim: Al-Ash'ath transmits Hasan's report that lying, breaking promises, and betraying trusts make someone a hypocrite even if he fasts, prays, and claims belief.
THALABI:v5p73/r2.anchor: الأشعث عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ثلاث من كن فيه

THALABI:v5p73/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v5p73/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud lists lying, breaking promises, and betraying covenants as signs of hypocrisy and says God confirmed this in the passage beginning with the one who made a covenant.
THALABI:v5p73/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود اعتبروا المنافق ثلاث: إذا حدث كذب، وإذا وعد أخلف،

THALABI:v5p73/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p73/r4.claim: The author warns that the report's apparent meaning is difficult and that someone who does not know its interpretation will make a serious error.
THALABI:v5p73/r4.anchor: وهذا خبر صعب الظاهر. فمن لم يعلم تأويله عظم خطؤه وتفسيره.

THALABI:v5p73/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r5.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p73/r5.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan recounts hearing Abu Hurayra transmit a Prophetic version with three signs—lying, betrayal of trust, and breaking promises—which left him fearing for himself and everyone.
THALABI:v5p73/r5.anchor: قال: حدثنا عمار بن قيراط عن بكير بن معروف عن مقاتل بن حيان قال: كنت على قضاء سمرقند

THALABI:v5p73/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p73/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v5p73/r6.claim: Distressed by the report, Muqatil left his judicial post and sought answers from scholars in Bukhara, Merv, and Nishapur; Shahr ibn Hawshab advised him to ask Sa'id ibn Jubayr in Ray.
THALABI:v5p73/r6.anchor: فتوزع فيه فكري وانقسم قلبي وخفت على نفسي وعلى جميع الناس وقلت من ينجو

THALABI:v5p74/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v5p74/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr tells Muqatil that he too fears these traits and directs him to Hasan al-Basri, hoping Hasan can resolve the question for them and Muslims.
THALABI:v5p74/r1.anchor: فقال: أنا كذلك خائف على نفسي منذ بلغني هذا الخبر، وأنا خائف عليك وعلى نفسي من هذه الخصال:

THALABI:v5p74/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
THALABI:v5p74/r2.claim: Hasan says Shahr heard only half the report: the Prophet's companions feared its implications, Fatima conveyed their concern, and the Prophet clarified at a public gathering that he meant hypocrites specifically.
THALABI:v5p74/r2.anchor: فقال رحم الله شهرا قد بلغها النصف من الخبر ولم يبلغهما النصف، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v5p74/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r3.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p74/r3.claim: The Prophet explains that the lying referred to hypocrites who claimed their faith and inward confirmation matched his, as exposed in the declaration that they bear witness to his prophethood.
THALABI:v5p74/r3.anchor: فإن المنافقين أتوني وقالوا لي: والله إن إيماننا كإيمانك وتصديق قلوبنا كتصديق قلبك

THALABI:v5p74/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r4.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p74/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies the trust as prayer and the whole religion, linking betrayal to hypocrites' lazy, ostentatious prayer and to the warning against those heedless of prayer.
THALABI:v5p74/r4.anchor: وأما قولي: إذا أؤتمن خان: فإن الأمانة الصلاة والدين كله أمانة، قال الله تعالى:

THALABI:v5p74/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r5.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p74/r5.claim: The Prophet relates broken promise to Tha'laba, who asked for a blessing on his flock, became wealthy, then refused the requested charity; the clarification relieved the companions, who donated generously.
THALABI:v5p74/r5.anchor: وأما قولي: إذا وعد أخلف، فإن ثعلبة بن حاطب أتاني فقال:

THALABI:v5p74/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p74/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p74/r6.claim: Hasan also transmits a version stating that lying, breaking promises, and betraying a trust mark a hypocrite even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be Muslim.
THALABI:v5p74/r6.anchor: وروى القاسم بن بشر عن أسامة عن محمد [المخرمي] قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

THALABI:v5p75/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p75/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v5p75/r1.claim: Hasan asks whether an indebted person who promises repayment when he lacks the means, then fails to pay at the beginning of the month, thereby becomes a hypocrite.
THALABI:v5p75/r1.anchor: فقال الحسن: يا أبا سعيد والله لئن كان لرجل علي دين فلقيني فتقاضاني وليس عندي

THALABI:v5p75/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p75/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
THALABI:v5p75/r2.claim: Hasan recounts that a man near death urged that the person he had promised be married, fearing he would meet God with one-third of hypocrisy; Hasan questions whether a person can be one-third hypocrite.
THALABI:v5p75/r2.anchor: ثم حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن أباه لما حضره الموت قال: زوجوا فلانا فإني وعدته أن أزوجه

THALABI:v5p75/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p75/r3.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
THALABI:v5p75/r3.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah challenges a blanket reading by asking whether Joseph's brothers, who lied, broke a promise, and betrayed trust, were hypocrites despite their prophetic family.
THALABI:v5p75/r3.anchor: فقال لي أعجزت أن تقول له: أخبرني عن إخوة يوسف ألم يعدوا أباهم فأخلفوه

THALABI:v5p75/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p75/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v5p75/r4.claim: Jabir explains that the Prophet meant particular hypocrites who lied to him, betrayed his confidence, and promised to accompany him on campaign but failed to go.
THALABI:v5p75/r4.anchor: فقال: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما قال هذا الحديث في المنافقين

THALABI:v5p75/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p75/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p75/r6.claim: The account links the hypocrites' broken pledge to the revelation about those who covenanted to give charity and then lied, and Hasan accepts Ata's explanation that the hadith addresses hypocrites specifically.
THALABI:v5p75/r6.anchor: وأنزل في المنافقين ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا إلى قوله تعالى: بما كانوا يكذبون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:75-77/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:75-77/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:75-77/r3.claim: When God gave them His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:75-77/r3.anchor: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به

ELMALILI:9:75-77/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r1.claim: The passage is reported to have been revealed about Saʿlaba ibn Hatib; after the Prophet warned him that little faithfully paid is better than much he could not bear, Saʿlaba renewed his request and vowed to give every rights-holder their due.
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r1.anchor: Bunun da Sa‘lebe b. Hâtıb sebebiyle nâzil olduğu mervîdir. Şöyle ki Sa‘lebe Peygamber’in huzûruna gelmiş

ELMALILI:9:75-77/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r2.claim: Saʿlaba's flock multiplied until Medina could not contain it; he moved to a valley and stopped attending the congregation and Friday prayer.
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r2.anchor: derken üredikçe üremiş Medine dar gelir olmuş, bir vâdiye gitmiş ve cemaat ve cumadan kesilmiş.

ELMALILI:9:75-77/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r3.claim: When the Prophet's collectors asked Saʿlaba for the prescribed alms, he called them like the jizya and said he would think about paying, illustrating the withholding and turning away.
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r3.anchor: Sa‘lebe’ye uğrayıp Resûlullah’ın ferâizi mübeyyin fermanını okuyarak sadakayı istediklerinde “bu cizyeler ne? Bunlar cizyenin kardeşi, hele siz gidin de düşüneyim” demiş

ELMALILI:9:75-77/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r4.claim: When the collectors returned, the Prophet twice lamented Saʿlaba before they spoke, and these verses were revealed.
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r4.anchor: Tahsildarlar[^1] dönüp Resûlullah’a geldiklerinde daha onlar bir şey söylemeden iki kere يَا وَيْحَ ثـَعْلَبَة buyurmuş, bu sebeple bu âyetler nâzil olmuş.

ELMALILI:9:75-77/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r5.claim: Afterward Saʿlaba brought the alms, but the Prophet refused it; Abu Bakr and Umar also refused it, and Saʿlaba died in Uthman's time, when the judgment of 9:77 had come to pass.
ELMALILI:9:75-77/r5.anchor: Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’e getirmiş kabul etmemiş, Hazret-i Ömer’e getirmiş kabul etmemiş ve Hazret-i Osman zamanında helâk olmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r1.claim: The commonly reported occasions of revelation for the first two verses conflict with historical evidence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r1.anchor: Bu âyetlerden ilk ikisinin nüzûl sebebi olarak tefsirlerde genellikle yer alan olayların tarihî verilerle bağdaşmadığı görülmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.claim: The passage exemplifies contradictions among people whose faith cannot discipline their conduct and points to hypocrisy in its context and timing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r2.anchor: nifak zihniyetine ve münafıkların tutumlarına gönderme yapılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r3.claim: Prophetic hadiths say deeds depend on intentions and that someone earns reward for intending good but being unable to do it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r3.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in hadislerinde amellerin niyetlere bağlı olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r4.claim: Hypocrites who turn to God for self-interest, promise charity if favored, then become miserly and turn away lose responsibility and cannot be trusted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:75/r4.anchor: sırf kendi çıkarının söz konusu olduğu durumda Allah’a yönelen, üstelik –beklentisine kavuşursa bunları– hayır yolunda kullanacağına dair Allah’a söz veren

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r14.claim: Some firmly covenanted with God to give charity and be righteous if enriched, then broke that covenant when their request was granted and remained trapped in hypocrisy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r14.anchor: منهم من أكد العقد مع الله ، ثم نقضه ، فلحقه شؤم ذلك ؛ فبقي خالدا في نفاقه

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r15.claim: In the outward legal sense, miserliness is withholding what is obligatory; each person’s miserliness also takes a form suited to that person’s state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r15.anchor: وحد البخل - على لسان العلم - منع الواجب . وبخل كل أحد على ما يليق بحاله

QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r16.claim: Preferring anything over God’s pleasure is miserliness: a miser with wealth loses its blessing, one who withholds the self from obedience loses health, and one who withholds the spirit from God is forsaken until life becomes misery.
QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r16.anchor: وكل من آثر شيئا من دون رضاء ربه فقد اتصف ببخله ، فمن يبخل بماله تزل عنه البركة

BURHAN:v3p381/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p381/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p381/r8.claim: Further examples use singular-form clauses followed by plural meaning, with when He gave them of His bounty, they were miserly cited as an exception.
BURHAN:v3p381/r8.anchor: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله

SULAMI:v1p282#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p282#3/r1.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p282#3/r1.claim: Abu Hafs defines stinginess as abandoning generosity when it is needed.

SULAMI:v1p282#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p282#3/r2.speaker: حمدون القصار
SULAMI:v1p282#3/r2.claim: Hamdun al-Qassar says whoever regards wealth as his own possession is miserly, since he keeps other people's hands away from it.
SULAMI:v1p282#3/r2.anchor: قال حمدون القصار : من رأى لنفسه ملكا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r2.claim: A weak report from Abu Umama says Thalaba promised charity if made wealthy, then expanded flocks led him to abandon congregational prayer; when collectors arrived he refused, and 9:75–77 was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن ثعلبة ابن حاطب قال يا رسول الله ادع الله أن يرزقني مالا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also transmits a version of the Thalaba story concerning the revelation of 9:75–77.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p120/r3.anchor: من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس نحوه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p253/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p253/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p253/r1.claim: The account says Tha'laba's flock multiplied after the Prophet prayed for his wealth, but he gradually abandoned congregational prayer and refused the collectors' demand for alms, unlike a man from Banu Sulaym who freely gave camels; the verses were revealed about Tha'laba's broken vow and lies.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p253/r1.anchor: حقه، فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - "اللهم ارزق ثعلبة مالا"، فاتخذ غنما فنمت كما ينمو الدود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r1.claim: A long account says Thalaba requested a prayer for wealth; despite advice that little he could thank God for was better, his flock multiplied, distracted him from prayer, and he called the collector's due a tax, prompting revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r1.anchor: وذكروا له حديثا طويلا وقد لخصت منه: أنه سأل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدعو الله أن يرزقه مالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r2.claim: After a relative informed him of the revelation, Thalaba brought his charity, but the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman refused it; he died during Uthman's caliphate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r2.anchor: فأخبره قريب له بها، فجاء بصدقته إلى الرسول فلم يقبلها، فلما قبض الرسول أتى أبا بكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r7.claim: Being stingy with it means withholding its due; whenever stinginess is followed by a threat, it denotes withholding an obligatory right.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p466/r7.anchor: بخلوا به أي: بإخراج حقه منه، وكل بخل أعقب بوعيد فهو عبارة عن منع الحق الواجب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r1.claim: When an official reported a man withholding zakat, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to leave him and let the contempt he incurs serve as punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p467/r1.anchor: وهذا نحو ما روي أن عاملا كتب إلى عمر بن عبد العزيز أن فلانا يمنع الزكاة، فكتب إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r1.claim: When God gave them from His bounty, they withheld the right due to God from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r1.anchor: أي منعوا حق الله تعالى منه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r2.claim: They turned away from obedience to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r2.anchor: أي أعرضوا عن طاعة الله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r3.claim: The final clause may be independent or circumstantial; their established habit of turning from obedience explains their conduct, and that continuing habit does not conflict with either syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r3.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة أو حالية والاستمرار المقتضى للتقدم لا ينافي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r4.claim: One explanation distinguishes an outward turning away in their bodies from inward aversion in their hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v10p144/r4.anchor: والمراد على ما قيل : تولوا بأجرامهم وهم معرضون بقلوبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet, before the two men could speak, lamented Thalaba twice and prayed for al-Sulami; after hearing what Thalaba had done, he refused his charity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r1.anchor: فلما رآهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يكلماه قال: يا ويح ثعلبة يا ويح ثعلبة، ثم دعا للسلمي بخير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r2.claim: Thalaba begged the Prophet to accept his charity; the Prophet said God had forbidden its acceptance, and told him this was the result of disobeying the earlier command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r2.anchor: إن الله عز وجل منعني أن أقبل منك صدقتك، فجعل يحثو التراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r3.claim: After the Prophet refused Thalaba's charity, Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān each also refused it; Thalaba died during ʿUthmān's caliphate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r3.anchor: لم يقبلها منك رسول الله ولا أبو بكر، أنا أقبلها منك؟ فلم يقبلها فلما ولي عثمان أتاه فلم يقبلها منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Qatāda say Thalaba promised charity, care for kin, and every due if given wealth, then inherited from a cousin but failed to keep his promise, occasioning the verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة: أتى ثعلبة مجلسا من الأنصار فأشهدهم لئن آتاني الله من فضله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r5.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujāhid say the verse concerns Thalaba ibn Ḥāṭib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, who publicly vowed charity if granted wealth and then withheld it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p76/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: نزلت في ثعلبة بن حاطب ومعتب بن قشير، وهما من بني عمرو بن عوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r1.claim: When God gave them from His bounty, they withheld the due owed to Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r1.anchor: بخلوا به } منعوا حق الله منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:76-78/r2.claim: They turned away from obedience and were habitually averse to it.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r6.claim: Repeating 'from His bounty' confirms the pledger's own wording and stresses that God owes no one anything and no creature can cause or control His gifts.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r6.anchor: وكرر قوله : { من فضله } تقريرا لما قاله المعاهد تأكيدا للإعلام بأنه لا حق عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r7.claim: They broke the emphatic pledge and withheld what was due, beyond merely failing to give voluntary secret charity.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r7.anchor: { بخلوا به } أي كذبوا فيما عاهدوا عليه وأكدوه غاية التأكد , فلم يتصدقوا بل منعوا الحق الواجب إظهاره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r8.claim: They forced themselves away from obeying the benefactor despite knowing the ugliness of breaking their pledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r8.anchor: { وتولوا } أي كلفوا أنفسهم الإعراض عن الطاعة لمن تفضل عليهم مع معرفتهم بقبح نقض العهد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r9.claim: Their turning away is in their hearts as well as their bodies; aversion was a settled trait already present when they made the pledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r9.anchor: { وهم معرضون * } اي بقلوبهم , والإعراض وصف لهم لازم لم يتجدد لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r11.claim: The passage escalates from ingratitude for a gift without a pledge to ingratitude after an explicit pledge, moving from the lesser offense to the greater.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r11.anchor: أن في الأولى كفران نعمة الغني من غير عهد , وفي هذه كفرانها مع العهد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r12.claim: The next verse's grave requital highlights how serious it is to betray a covenant (9:77).
BIQAI-FULL:v3p363/r12.anchor: ودل عظيم شأن العهد بتعظيم الجزاء على خيانته بقوله :

DURR-FULL:v4p247/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says three traits mark a hypocrite: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying a trust; he recites this passage about a covenant with God.
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: ثلاث من كن فيه فهو منافق إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا ائتمن خان وتلا هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v4p247/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet's saying that the hypocrite has three signs: lying, breaking promises, and betraying a trust.
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال آية المنافق ثلاث إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا ائتمن خان

DURR-FULL:v4p247/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r3.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb says he eventually found the three hypocrite traits across scripture: this passage for breaking a covenant and lying, 33:72 for the trust, and 63:1 for lying.
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: سمعت بالثلاث التي تذكر في المنافق إذا ائتمن خان وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا حدث كذب فالتمستها في الكتاب زمانا طويلا حتى سقطت عليها

DURR-FULL:v4p247/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says an Anṣārī promised God but, after inheriting his cousin's wealth, withheld it; breaking the promise brought him hypocrisy until he met God.
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r4.anchor: عن الحسن أن رجلا من الأنصار هو الذي قال هذا فمات ابن عم له فورث منه مالا فبخل به ولم يف الله بما عاهد عليه فأعقبه بذلك نفاقا

DURR-FULL:v4p247/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r5.speaker: أبو قلابة
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r5.claim: Abū Qilāba compares followers of sectarian desires to hypocrites: their words differ, but hypocrisy joins their cause; he cites 9:58 and 9:61 as well as this passage.
DURR-FULL:v4p247/r5.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال: مثل أصحاب الأهواء مثل المنافقين كلامهم شتى وجماع أمرهم النفاق ثم تلا {ومنهم من عاهد الله} {ومنهم من يلمزك}

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r1.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r1.claim: Thalaba asked the Prophet to pray for wealth, received abundant flocks, moved outside Medina, and gradually abandoned communal prayers until he attended only Friday prayer and sought news from travelers.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r1.anchor: عن ثعلبة بن حاطب : انه قال لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ادع الله ان يرزقني مالا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r2.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r2.claim: When collectors asked for his charity, Thalaba refused, calling it a levy like the poll tax, and told them to return later.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r2.anchor: فقال : ماهذه الا جزية ، ما هذه الا اخت الجزية ، ما ادري ماهذه ؟ انطلقا حتى تفرغا ثم عودا الي

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r3.speaker: السلمي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r3.claim: The man from Banu Sulaym selected good camels for charity and insisted that the collectors accept his payment.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r3.anchor: فانطلقا وسمع بهما السلمي فنظر إلى خيار اسنان ابله فعزلهما للصدقة ثم استقبلهم بها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r4.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r4.claim: After a relative told him the revelation concerned him, Thalaba tried to pay, but the Prophet said God had forbidden him from accepting it.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r4.anchor: فقال : ويح ياثعلبة قد انزل الله فيك كذا وكذا فخرج ثعلبة حتى اتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r5.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r5.claim: The account says the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman all refused Thalaba's later charity, and he died during Uthman's caliphate.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1847/r5.anchor: فلم يقبلها وهلك ثعلبة في خلافة عثمان رضي الله عنهم اجمعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r1.claim: A reported occasion says the passage concerns the hypocrite Thalaba b. Hatib, who sought the Prophet's prayer for wealth, became rich, refused alms on his livestock, repented, but the Prophet refused his offering; the report says it remained unaccepted through the first three caliphs until Thalaba died under Uthman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r1.anchor: قيل : نزلت في ثعلبة بن حاطب من المنافقين سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدعو له بسعة الرزق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r2.claim: Another attribution names Mu'attib b. Qushayr; on this account plural pronouns represent one person, with an individual's deed attached to his clan in Arab usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا فضمائر الجمع في لنصدقن وما بعده مراد بها واحد وإنما نسبت الفعل إلى جماعة المنافقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur also allows that Thalaba asked and some companions such as Mu'attib followed his example, received similar wealth, and became stingy, though no separate story about them is known.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن ثعلبة سأل ذلك فتبعه بعض أصحابه مثل معتب بن قشير فأوتي مثل ما أوتي ثعلبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r4.claim: The pledge to give alms explains the preceding covenant, and لنصدقن is assimilated from لنتصدقن for ease of pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r4.anchor: وجملة { لنصدقن } بيان لجملة { عاهد الله } وفعل { لنصدقن } أصله لنتصدقن فأدغم للتخفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r5.claim: Their turning away is from the covenant they made and from gratitude for their Lord's blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p272#2/r5.anchor: الإعراض : إعراضهم عن عهدهم وعن شكر نعمة ربهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r4.claim: After zakat became obligatory, collectors brought the Prophet’s written order for sheep; Thaʿlaba called it a sister of the jizya and asked time to decide.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r4.anchor: فلما بلغوا ثعلبة وقرأ الكتاب قال: هذه أخت الجزية، ثم قال لهم: دعوني حتى أرى رأيي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r5.claim: When collectors reported Thaʿlaba’s refusal, the Prophet said woe to him three times; after a relative informed him of the revelation, he offered zakat but the Prophet refused it by God’s order.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r5.anchor: قال «ويح ثعلبة» ثلاثا، ونزلت الآية فيه، فحضر القصة قريب لثعلبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r6.claim: Thaʿlaba later sought to pay zakat to Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, but each followed the Prophet’s refusal; Thaʿlaba died during ʿUthmān’s caliphate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p61/r6.anchor: ثم ورد ثعلبة على أبي بكر ثم على عمر ثم على عثمان يرغب إلى كل واحد منهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r1.claim: The bounty God gave them was the wealth they had requested.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ فلما آتاهم من فضله ﴾ أي ما طلبوا من المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r2.claim: They became miserly with the wealth and failed to fulfill their covenant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ بخلوا به ﴾ ولم يفوا بما عاهدوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p475#2/r3.claim: They turned away from their covenant.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.claim: Some hypocrites pledged that, if God enriched them, they would give charity and become righteous, but they did not fulfill their claim or give as they had promised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.anchor: ومن المنافقين من أعطى الله عهده وميثاقه: لئن أغناه من فضله ليصدقن من ماله، وليكونن من الصالحين. فما وفى بما قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan al-Basri, and many other commentators identify Tha'laba ibn Hatib al-Ansari as the occasion for revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.anchor: منهم ابن عباس، والحسن البصري: أن سبب نزول هذه الآية الكريمة في "ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.claim: In a report through Abu Umama, Tha'laba asks the Prophet for wealth; the Prophet says a little wealth whose thanks he can render is better than much he cannot bear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري، أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادع الله أن يرزقني مالا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.claim: Tha'laba renews his request, promises to give everyone their due, receives the Prophet's prayer for wealth, and his flock multiplies until he leaves Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.claim: As the flock grows, Tha'laba first prays only noon and afternoon in congregation, then only Friday, and eventually leaves Friday prayer too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.claim: After zakah is prescribed, the Prophet sends two collectors; Tha'laba refuses, calling it a tax like jizya, while a man of Sulaym gladly gives his best camels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.claim: The Sulami donor voluntarily gives his choice camels, and the collectors accept them after he insists they take the charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.claim: The Prophet foretells Tha'laba's failure, then refuses his later charity; Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman also refuse it, and Tha'laba dies during Uthman's caliphate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي، عن ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.claim: The story reports that the command to take charity in 9:103 was revealed in connection with Tha'laba's case.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.anchor: وأنزل الله جل ثناؤه: {خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها} الآية

JISHUMI:v5p3202/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r2.claim: They found no fault to criticize except that God enriched them from His bounty.
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r2.anchor: وتدل أن القوم لم يجدوا مغمزا ولا مطعنا إلا أن أغناهم الله من فضله.

JISHUMI:v5p3202/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r4.claim: Those who turn away from repentance and obedience face only punishment; this warning encourages obedience and deters sin.
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن كل من تولى عن التوبة وطاعة الله ليس له إلا العذاب، وذلك ترغيب في الطاعة، وزجر عن المعصية.

JISHUMI:v5p3202/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r8.claim: Bukhl is withholding what one could give; in religious usage it means withholding an obligation, since miserliness is a deficiency.
JISHUMI:v5p3202/r8.anchor: والبخل: منع النائل، وقد صار في الشرع اسما لمنع الواجب؛ لأن البخل صفة نقص.

MUQATIL:9:75-79/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:75-79/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:75-79/r3.claim: When God granted the hypocrites bounty, they withheld it and turned away in refusal.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r1.claim: God gave them wealth and they attained what they wished for.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r2.claim: They withheld God’s due and did not fulfill their covenant.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r2.anchor: منعوا حق الله ولم يفوا بالعهد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r3.claim: They turned from obedience to God and persisted in their aversion.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p100#3/r3.anchor: عن طاعة الله ﴿ وهم معرضون ﴾ مصرون على الاعراض

QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r10.claim: Ātāhum min faḍlihi means God gave them from His bounty.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r11.claim: Their miserliness means withholding charity, spending on good, and fulfilling what they promised and undertook.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r11.anchor: أي بإعطاء الصدقة وبإنفاق المال في الخير، وبالوفاء بما ضمنوا والتزموا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r12.claim: Tawallaw means turning away from obedience to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r13.claim: They openly turned away from Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:75-77#2/r13.anchor: أي عن الإسلام، أي مظهرون للإعراض عنه

BURSEVI:v3p356/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356/r1.claim: After God gave them wealth from His bounty, they withheld its due, abandoned obedience and their covenant, and remained habitual turnaways.

BURSEVI:v3p356/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v3p356/r2.claim: When the collectors returned, the Prophet said woe to Thalaba twice before they told him what had happened; Umar then warned Thalaba that revelation had condemned him.
BURSEVI:v3p356/r2.anchor: فلما رجعا قال لهما رسول الله قبل أن يكلماه "يا ويح ثعلبة" مرتين

BURSEVI:v3p356/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p356/r3.claim: Thalaba brought the alms, but the Prophet refused it because God had forbidden acceptance; the Prophet called this the recompense for Thalaba’s refusal and calling it a tax.
BURSEVI:v3p356/r3.anchor: فجاء ثعلبة بالصدقة فقال عليه السلام : "إن الله منعني أن أقبل منك

BURSEVI:v3p356/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p356/r4.claim: Thalaba’s distress over rejection was attributed to public shame, not repentance from hypocrisy; Abu Bakr and Umar also refused his later payments, and he died under Uthman.
BURSEVI:v3p356/r4.anchor: لا لأنه تاب عن النفاق بل للحوق العار من عدم قبول زكاته مع المسلمين

BURSEVI:v3p356/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p356/r5.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p356/r5.claim: Al-Haddadi states that Uthman did not accept Thalaba’s charity.
BURSEVI:v3p356/r5.anchor: قال الحدادي : لم يقبل منه عثمان صدقته انتهى

RAZI-FULL:v16p112#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p112#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p112#2/r4.claim: Razi identifies three traits: miserliness, meaning withholding a right; turning away from the pledge; and disregarding God's duties and commands.
RAZI-FULL:v16p112#2/r4.anchor: وصفهم بصفات ثلاثة : الصفة الأولى : البخل وهو عبارة عن منع الحق
